chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Maliki narrated to us; he said: Ahmad ibn Hilal al-Abarta'i narrated to us; he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
"Fast in Sha'ban and perform ghusl on the night of its middle,
"that is a lightening from your Lord."
"Then he said: And the ghusl of the one making up the salat of the eclipse, due to having deliberately abandoned it, is sunnah (prophetic tradition). This indicates that."

key_terms.تَخْفِيفٌ: A lightening or easing granted by Allah
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: A recommended practice from the sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.صُومُوا: Observe fasting as an act of worship
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ ٱلنِّصْفِ: The night of the middle of the month

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about fasting in Sha'ban, the ghusl of mid-Sha'ban, and making up the eclipse prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs fasting in Sha'ban and performing ghusl on the night of the middle of Sha'ban, presenting it as a divinely granted ease. It also states that ghusl for one who makes up the eclipse prayer after deliberately neglecting it is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), indicating a recommended ritual act within jurisprudential practice.
